questions.q: Fill up: PID is defined as infection of the ____ female genital tract.
questions.exp: Page 184: 'Definition: Infection of upper female genital tract'.

questions.q: Which three anatomical sites are listed as being included in PID?
questions.exp: 'Includes: Endometritis (uterus), Salpingitis (Fallopian tubes), Oophoritis (Ovaries)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common route of spread is an ascending infection travelling along with ____.
questions.exp: 'm/c route of spread: Ascending infection along with sperms (STDs)'.

questions.q: PID is most commonly seen in:
opts: Sexually active females aged 15 to 35 years
Pregnant women in the third trimester
questions.exp: 'm/c seen in: Sexually active females (15-35 yrs)'.

questions.q: Fill up: PID is described as a ____ infection.
questions.exp: 'PID: Polymicrobial infection'.

questions.q: True/False: PID is an infection confined to the lower genital tract.
opts: True - it begins in the vagina
True - the cervix is the upper limit
questions.exp: It is defined as infection of the upper female genital tract.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT one of the three components printed under 'includes'?
questions.exp: Cervicitis has its own chapter; PID includes endometritis, salpingitis and oophoritis.

questions.q: Fill up: Insertion of a copper T within ____ weeks is a risk factor.
questions.exp: 'CuT insertion (< 3 weeks)'.

questions.q: Which four obstetric or procedural risk factors are printed?
opts: Post abortion, caesarean section, nulliparity and endometriosis
Post abortion, post partum, history of instrumentation and previous history of PID
Post partum, lactation, sterilisation and fibroid
questions.exp: The risk factor list prints 'multiple risk factors', post abortion, post partum, H/o instrumentation, previous H/o PID and CuT insertion.

questions.q: Which two protective factors are printed?
opts: Oral contraceptive pills and depot medroxyprogesterone
questions.exp: 'Protective in PID: Barrier contraceptives (Condoms), MIRENA'.

questions.q: Fill up: Infection can spread to the abdomen causing peritonitis and ____.
questions.exp: 'Infection can spread to abdomen: 1. Peritonitis, 2. Perihepatitis'.

questions.q: Which intrauterine device is printed as protective?
questions.exp: MIRENA appears under the protective list.

questions.q: Match the factor with its category - 1) Condoms 2) CuT insertion within 3 weeks 3) Post partum state 4) MIRENA ... A) Risk factor B) Protective
questions.exp: Condoms and MIRENA protect; recent CuT insertion and the post partum state increase risk.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman had a copper T inserted 10 days ago and now has lower abdominal pain and fever. Which printed risk factor applies?
questions.exp: Insertion within 3 weeks is explicitly listed as a risk factor.

questions.q: True/False: The copper T is listed as protective against PID.
opts: True - after 3 weeks it becomes protective
True - it is protective in the MIRENA form
questions.exp: Recent CuT insertion is a risk factor; MIRENA is the protective device.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed risk factor for PID?
questions.exp: Barrier contraceptives are protective, not a risk factor.

questions.q: Fill up: The first step in the printed pathogenesis is ____ of the uterus.
questions.exp: 'Pathogenesis: 1. Uterus: Endometritis'.

questions.q: Which three symptoms are printed alongside endometritis?
opts: Menstrual abnormalities, dysmenorrhoea and lower abdominal pain
questions.exp: The uterus block lists menstrual abnormalities, dysmenorrhoea, lower abdominal pain and endometrial biopsy.

questions.q: Which investigation is printed in the endometritis block?
questions.exp: 'Endometrial biopsy' is listed in the uterus block.

questions.q: How are the fallopian tubes described in salpingitis?
questions.exp: 'Thick, congested, hyperemic, swollen tubes'.

questions.q: Fill up: Inflammation of the tubal lining is called ____.
questions.exp: 'Endosalpingitis'.

questions.q: Which two late tubal outcomes are printed under the tubes heading?
questions.exp: 'Pyosalpinx' and 'Hydrosalpinx'.

questions.q: Fill up: The third step in the pathogenesis is ____ of the ovaries.
questions.exp: '3. Oophoritis'.

questions.q: The fourth step is:
questions.exp: '4. Peritonitis + pelvic abscess'.

questions.q: In women of reproductive age, which two organisms are most commonly implicated and in what order?
questions.exp: 'Reproductive age: Chlamydia > Gonorrhea'.

questions.q: Fill up: In virgins, PID is caused by genital ____ spreading by the haematogenous route.
questions.exp: 'Virgins: Genital TB (Hematogenous)'.

questions.q: Which organism is named for menopausal females?
questions.exp: 'menopausal females: E. coli'.

questions.q: Fill up: In copper IUD users, the organism named is ____.
questions.exp: 'Cu-IUD users: Actinomyces'.

questions.q: Match each population with its organism - 1) Reproductive age 2) Virgins 3) Menopausal females 4) Cu-IUD users ... A) Actinomyces B) Chlamydia more than gonorrhoea C) E. coli D) Genital TB
questions.exp: Reproductive age is chlamydia then gonorrhoea; virgins have haematogenous TB; menopausal women have E. coli; Cu-IUD users have Actinomyces.

questions.q: Scenario: A 58-year-old woman presents with a tubo-ovarian abscess. Which organism does the printed list favour?
questions.exp: Menopausal females are listed with E. coli.

questions.q: True/False: In virgins, PID is most often due to ascending chlamydial infection.
opts: True - virgins have the highest chlamydia rate
questions.exp: In virgins the printed cause is genital tuberculosis by the haematogenous route.

questions.q: Odd one out - which organism is NOT in the printed 'most common PID' list?
questions.exp: Gardnerella causes bacterial vaginosis, not PID.

questions.q: Which symptom is printed as the most common?
questions.exp: 'm/c: Lower abdominal pain (B/L)'.

questions.q: Fill up: Pain during ____ is increased.
questions.exp: '↑ Pain during coitus'.

questions.q: What does fever lead to in the acute phase?
questions.exp: The acute phase arrow reads 'Fever → menorrhagia'.

questions.q: Which two bleeding patterns are printed under AUB?
questions.exp: 'AUB: Intermenstrual bleed, Postcoital bleed'.

questions.q: Fill up: ____ is a long-term feature listed among the clinical features.
questions.exp: 'Infertility'.

questions.q: Fill up: The perihepatitis of PID is Fitz-Hugh-____ syndrome.
questions.exp: 'Complication: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis Syndrome: Perihepatitis'.

questions.q: The adhesions of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome are described as:
opts: Violin string adhesions between the liver capsule and anterior abdominal wall
Bands between the uterus and bladder
questions.exp: 'Violin string adhesions: Between liver capsule & anterior abdominal wall'.

questions.q: Fill up: The pain of perihepatitis is in the ____ upper quadrant.
questions.exp: 'C/o right upper quadrant pain'.

questions.q: Which organism order is given for Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome?
questions.exp: 'm/c Chlamydia > Gonorrhea'.

questions.q: How is the diagnosis of PID described?
questions.exp: 'PID: Clinical diagnosis'.

questions.q: Match each clinical feature with its descriptor - 1) Lower abdominal pain 2) Fever in the acute phase 3) Intermenstrual bleed 4) Perihepatitis ... A) Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome B) Most common, bilateral C) Menorrhagia D) AUB
questions.exp: Bilateral lower abdominal pain is commonest; fever drives menorrhagia; intermenstrual bleeding is AUB; perihepatitis is Fitz-Hugh-Curtis.

questions.q: Scenario: A young woman with PID complains of right upper quadrant pain. What is the printed explanation?
opts: Perihepatitis with violin string adhesions - Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome
questions.exp: Right upper quadrant pain is the Fitz-Hugh-Curtis presentation.

questions.q: True/False: The violin string adhesions of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome lie between the liver capsule and the diaphragm.
questions.exp: They are printed between the liver capsule and the anterior abdominal wall.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed PID feature?
questions.exp: Haemoptysis is not among the printed features.

questions.q: Fill up: On USG, a tubo-ovarian ____ is one of the two findings.
questions.exp: '1. USG: Tubo-ovarian mass'.

questions.q: The second USG finding is:
questions.exp: 'Swollen tubes'.

questions.q: Which three ultrasound signs are printed?
opts: Whirlpool sign, target sign and cogwheel sign
Waist sign, bead on string sign and cogwheel sign
Snowstorm sign, bead on string and waist sign
String of pearls, waist sign and cogwheel sign
questions.exp: The signs block lists waist sign, bead on string sign and cogwheel sign.

questions.q: Fill up: The waist sign is associated with ____.
questions.exp: The figure caption prints 'Waist sign (Hydrosalpinx)'.

questions.q: The cogwheel sign is produced by:
questions.exp: 'Cogwheel sign (Thickened endosalpingeal walls)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The beads-on-string sign is illustrated under the ____ section.
questions.exp: The note reads 'USG: PID / Beads on string' and 'HSG: Genital TB'.

questions.q: What does endometrial biopsy demonstrate in PID?
questions.exp: '2. Endometrial biopsy: Endometritis'.

questions.q: Fill up: The gold standard investigation is ____.
questions.exp: '3. Laparoscopy: Gold standard'.

questions.q: Which three roles are printed for laparoscopy?
opts: Direct visualisation of tubes, adnexa and uterus; specimen collection; scoring for conception
Drainage of abscess, fulguration and biopsy
questions.exp: 'Visualize tubes, adnexa, uterus directly; Specimen collection; Scoring for conception'.

questions.q: Fill up: The CDC minimum criteria require lower abdominal pain plus any ____ of the three per-vaginal findings.
questions.exp: 'Lower abdominal pain with any 1 of the following P/v findings'.

questions.q: Which three per-vaginal findings make up the minimum criteria?
opts: Uterine tenderness, adnexal mass and fever
Cervical motion tenderness, discharge and fever
Cervical movement tenderness, adnexal tenderness and uterine tenderness
Adnexal tenderness, cervical erosion and discharge
questions.exp: The minimal criteria list cervical movement tenderness, adnexal tenderness and uterine tenderness.

questions.q: Fill up: The temperature threshold in the additional criteria is above ____ degrees Fahrenheit.
Which two laboratory markers are listed in the additional criteria?
questions.exp: 'ESR' and 'CRP' are printed in the additional criteria.

questions.q: Which microscopy finding is an additional criterion?
opts: Abundant white blood cells on saline microscopy of vaginal discharge
questions.exp: 'Saline microscopy of vaginal discharge: Abundant WBCs'.

questions.q: Fill up: The surest sign of PID at laparoscopy is pus trickling from the ____ end.
questions.exp: 'Surest sign of PID: Pus trickling from fimbrial end during laparoscopy'.

questions.q: Which scoring system is used in PID and what is excluded from it?
opts: Nugent score, which excludes clue cells
Boer-Meisel score, which does not include the type of organism
questions.exp: 'Scoring system for conception in PID: Boer-Meisel score (Type of organism not included)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The staging system named for PID is ____ staging.
questions.exp: 'Staging of PID: Gainesville staging'.

questions.q: What procedure is named for drainage of a pelvic abscess?
questions.exp: 'Culpotomy: Drainage of pelvic abscess'.

questions.q: Which two conditions must be ruled out in the differential?
opts: Urinary tract infection and renal colic
questions.exp: The D/d block prints ectopic pregnancy and appendicitis.

questions.q: Match each investigation with its role - 1) USG 2) Endometrial biopsy 3) Laparoscopy ... A) Gold standard B) Tubo-ovarian mass and swollen tubes C) Endometritis
questions.exp: USG shows the mass and swelling; biopsy shows endometritis; laparoscopy is the gold standard.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has lower abdominal pain and adnexal tenderness but no fever, discharge or raised ESR. Does she meet CDC criteria?
opts: Yes - she meets the minimum criteria for PID
No - all three per-vaginal findings are needed
No - a raised CRP is required
questions.exp: Lower abdominal pain with any one per-vaginal finding satisfies the minimum criteria.

questions.q: True/False: The beads-on-string sign is described here as an HSG finding of genital tuberculosis.
opts: False - it is an ultrasound sign of PID
questions.exp: The note prints 'USG: PID / Beads on string' and 'HSG: Genital TB'.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed ultrasound sign of PID?
questions.exp: Lead pipe appearance is an HSG description from the genital tuberculosis chapter.

questions.q: Fill up: Routine management of PID is on an ____ basis.
questions.exp: 'management: OPD basis'.

questions.q: Which three drugs make up the printed broad-spectrum regimen?
questions.exp: Inj. Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose + Tab Doxycycline 100 mg BD x 14 days + Tab metronidazole 400 mg BD x 14 days.

questions.q: Fill up: Ceftriaxone is given as ____ mg intramuscularly in a single dose.
questions.exp: 'Inj. Ceftriaxone 250mg IM single dose'.

questions.q: For how many days are doxycycline and metronidazole continued?
questions.exp: Both are printed as BD for 14 days.

questions.q: Fill up: Doxycycline is given at ____ mg twice daily.
questions.exp: 'Tab Doxycycline 100mg BD x 14 days'.

questions.q: Fill up: Metronidazole is given at ____ mg twice daily for 14 days.
questions.exp: 'Tab metronidazole 400mg BD x 14 days'.

questions.q: Which of the four admission indications relates to treatment failure?
questions.exp: '1. Not responding to oral treatment'.

questions.q: How many indications for admission are printed?
questions.exp: Not responding to oral treatment, pelvic abscess, pregnant with severe disease, pregnant and unable to take oral medication.

questions.q: Which two pregnancy-related indications are printed?
opts: Clinically severe disease, and inability to take oral medications
questions.exp: Both pregnancy indications are severe disease and inability to take oral drugs.

questions.q: Fill up: Intravenous antibiotics are continued for ____ hours after the patient becomes afebrile.
questions.exp: 'IV antibiotics continued for 24 hrs after patient becomes afebrile'.

questions.q: After the patient becomes afebrile, oral antibiotics are given for:
questions.exp: 'Oral antibiotics x 14 days'.

questions.q: Fill up: The first numbered long-term consequence of PID on this page is ____, described as the most common.
questions.exp: '1. Infertility: m/c'.

questions.q: How many numbered consequences are printed in that list?
questions.exp: Infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain, hydrosalpinx, recurrent PID and Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome.

questions.q: Which consequence is numbered fourth?
questions.exp: '4. Hydrosalpinx'.

questions.q: Fill up: The sixth item in the list is Fitz-Hugh-____ syndrome.
questions.exp: '6. Fitz-Hugh Curtis syndrome'.

questions.q: Advice on sexual activity after treatment is abstinence for:
questions.exp: 'Abstinence x 7-14 days'.

questions.q: Why is alcohol to be avoided?
opts: Because metronidazole is part of the regimen
questions.exp: The advice prints 'Avoid alcohol (metronidazole)'.

questions.q: Match each management element with its detail - 1) Ceftriaxone 2) Doxycycline 3) Metronidazole 4) IV antibiotics ... A) 400 mg BD x 14 days B) 250 mg IM single dose C) Continued 24 hours after fever settles D) 100 mg BD x 14 days
questions.exp: Ceftriaxone single IM dose, doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days, IV therapy until 24 hours afebrile.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with PID is admitted with a pelvic abscess. She defervesces on day 3. When can intravenous antibiotics stop?
opts: After a further 24 hours, then switch to oral therapy for 14 days
questions.exp: IV antibiotics are continued for 24 hours after the patient becomes afebrile, then oral for 14 days.

questions.q: True/False: Metronidazole is given as a single 2 g dose in the PID regimen.
questions.exp: It is 400 mg twice daily for 14 days.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT printed advice after PID treatment?
questions.exp: Dairy avoidance is not printed; alcohol avoidance is.

questions.q: Fill up: In the syndromic approach the patient receives yellow kit number ____.
questions.exp: 'No. 6: Yellow kit'.

questions.q: Which three drugs are printed for the patient in the syndromic regimen?
opts: Cefixime 400 mg stat, azithromycin 1 g and secnidazole 2 g
Cefixime 400 mg stat, metronidazole 400 mg BD for 14 days and doxycycline 100 mg BD for 14 days
Ceftriaxone 250 mg, doxycycline 100 mg and azithromycin 1 g
Azithromycin 1 g, cefixime 400 mg and metronidazole 400 mg
questions.exp: The patient regimen prints those three drugs.

questions.q: Fill up: The partner receives grey kit number ____.
questions.exp: 'Partner: No. 1: Grey kit'.

questions.q: What two drugs does the partner receive?
opts: Cefixime 400 mg single dose and azithromycin 1 g
questions.exp: The partner block prints cefixime single dose and azithromycin.

questions.q: Which mandatory exclusion is printed before starting the syndromic kit?
opts: Ensure the urine pregnancy test is negative
questions.exp: 'Ensure uPT (-)'.

questions.q: Which three per-vaginal findings trigger the syndromic PID kit?
opts: Uterine tenderness, cervical motion tenderness and adnexal tenderness
Uterine enlargement, adnexal mass and cervical erosion
Cervical motion tenderness, discharge and fever
Adnexal tenderness, abdominal rigidity and rebound
questions.exp: The indications list any one of uterine, cervical motion or adnexal tenderness.

questions.q: Fill up: The syndromic advice includes abstinence and the use of ____.
questions.exp: 'Advice: Abstinence x 7-14 days, Use of condoms'.

questions.q: Match each kit with its recipient - 1) Patient 2) Partner ... A) Grey kit 1 B) Yellow kit 6
questions.exp: The patient takes yellow kit 6 and the partner grey kit 1.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with lower abdominal pain and cervical motion tenderness has a positive urine pregnancy test. What is the printed next step?
opts: Rule out ectopic pregnancy before using the PID kit
questions.exp: 'Ensure uPT (-)' and the standing instruction to rule out ectopic pregnancy precede kit use.

questions.q: True/False: In the syndromic approach, the partner receives the same yellow kit as the patient.
opts: True - the partner receives double the dose
questions.exp: The partner receives grey kit 1 with cefixime and azithromycin.

questions.q: Odd one out - which drug is NOT in the syndromic PID patient kit?
questions.exp: Azithromycin is in the partner's grey kit, not the patient's yellow kit.

questions.q: Fill up: The pathogenesis is numbered through uterus, tubes, ovaries and finally peritonitis with pelvic ____.
questions.exp: Step 4 prints 'Peritonitis + pelvic abscess'.

questions.q: Which phrase describes the tubal appearance in salpingitis?
opts: Dilated with a lead pipe outline
questions.exp: The printed descriptors are thick, congested, hyperemic and swollen.

questions.q: Fill up: In reproductive-age women, chlamydia exceeds ____ as a cause of PID.
questions.exp: Printed: 'Reproductive age: Chlamydia > Gonorrhea'.

questions.q: Which organism is specifically linked to copper IUD use in the printed list?
questions.exp: 'Cu-IUD users: Actinomyces'.

questions.q: Fill up: The waist sign is captioned as ____ and the cogwheel sign as thickened endosalpingeal walls.
questions.exp: The caption prints 'Waist sign (Hydrosalpinx)'.

questions.q: Which investigation pairs with 'beads on string' in the printed note?
questions.exp: The note prints 'USG: PID / Beads on string' and 'HSG: Genital TB'.

questions.q: Which statement about HSG in this chapter is correct?
opts: HSG is the gold standard for PID
HSG belongs to the genital tuberculosis chapter, not to PID diagnostics here
HSG is the screening test for PID
questions.exp: The note assigns HSG to genital TB; PID imaging is by USG.

questions.q: Fill up: The laparoscopy note says the operator can visualise tubes, adnexa and ____ directly.
questions.exp: 'Visualize tubes, adnexa, uterus directly'.

questions.q: Which two diagnoses must be excluded before labelling pelvic pain as PID?
questions.exp: The D/d block lists ectopic pregnancy and appendicitis.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness and a temperature of 101.5 degrees Fahrenheit. Which CDC tier is satisfied?
opts: Both the minimum criteria and the additional criteria
questions.exp: Pain plus cervical motion tenderness meets the minimum criteria, and the temperature above 101 F meets an additional criterion.

questions.q: True/False: A raised ESR and CRP are part of the CDC minimum criteria for PID.
questions.exp: They belong to the additional criteria.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT among the three per-vaginal minimum-criteria findings?
questions.exp: A mass is not a minimum criterion; tenderness findings are.

questions.q: Fill up: The intramuscular cephalosporin in the OPD regimen is ____, given as a single dose.
questions.exp: 'Inj. Ceftriaxone 250mg IM single dose'.

questions.q: Which two oral antibiotics in the OPD regimen share the same 14-day duration?
questions.exp: Both are printed as twice daily for 14 days.

questions.q: Fill up: Pelvic ____ is the second indication for admission.
questions.exp: '2. Pelvic abscess'.

questions.q: Why is pregnancy singled out among the admission indications?
opts: Severe disease or inability to take oral medication in pregnancy warrants admission
questions.exp: Both pregnancy indications are clinical severity and inability to take oral drugs.

questions.q: Fill up: The list of six consequences begins with infertility and ends with Fitz-Hugh-Curtis ____.
questions.exp: Item 6 is Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome.

questions.q: Which two of the six consequences directly reflect tubal damage?
opts: Chronic pelvic pain and recurrent PID
questions.exp: Tubal damage produces infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

questions.q: Fill up: Alcohol is to be avoided because of the ____ in the regimen.
questions.exp: 'Avoid alcohol (metronidazole)'.

questions.q: What is the printed duration of abstinence after PID treatment?
questions.exp: 'Abstinence x 7-14 days'.

questions.q: Fill up: The syndromic patient kit is yellow kit 6; the partner kit is grey kit ____.
questions.exp: Partner: No. 1 grey kit.

questions.q: Which drug is common to the OPD regimen and the syndromic patient kit?
questions.exp: Metronidazole 400 mg BD appears in both the OPD regimen and yellow kit 6.

questions.q: Which drug appears in the partner kit but not in the patient's yellow kit?
questions.exp: The partner receives cefixime plus azithromycin; the patient receives cefixime, metronidazole and doxycycline.

questions.q: Match each PID consequence with its number - 1) Infertility 2) Ectopic pregnancy 3) Chronic pelvic pain 4) Recurrent PID ... A) 5 B) 2 C) 1 (m/c) D) 3
questions.exp: Infertility is 1 and most common; ectopic pregnancy 2; chronic pelvic pain 3; recurrent PID 5.

questions.q: Scenario: A patient with PID has completed 24 hours without fever on intravenous antibiotics. What is the printed next step?
opts: Switch to oral antibiotics for a total of 14 days
Continue intravenous therapy for another 7 days
questions.exp: IV therapy continues 24 hours past defervescence, then oral antibiotics for 14 days.

questions.q: True/False: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome appears both as an acute complication on the features page and as item 6 in the consequence list.
opts: False - it appears only on the features page
False - it appears only in the consequences list
questions.exp: It is printed under complications on p185 and again as item 6 on p187.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed admission indication?
opts: Pregnant patient unable to take oral medication
questions.exp: Hydrosalpinx is a numbered consequence, not an admission indication.
